Your fragment: {fragment}
Another resident holds the other fragment. Only the public board is open on this level:

Your fragment: {fragment}

levels.title: The circle

Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap by {overlap} characters.
Your fragment: {fragment}

{leader} founds the team group with createGroup and adds the others with addGroupMember.
Everyone else waits to be added.

A group has a treasury: depositGroup pays points in, only the treasurer can withdraw,
and whatever is left at the end of the run is split among the members.

levels.title: The second door
levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap, every seam by the same number of characters; the city does not say how many.
Your fragment: {fragment}
Your team is the same as on the last level: {members}.
Your group from that level still exists; check it with listMyGroups. If it is gone, {leader} founds a new one.
Every channel is open now, but messages cost marks.
Every transfer and every delivered DM leaves a receipt (see getStatus); showReceipt shows one, verified by the city, on the board or privately to one resident, for 1 mark.
You need every fragment of your team, and your team needs yours: whoever falls behind holds the others back.
Within an act, wrong passwords cost 2, 4, 6, then 8 points, one after another (your next one: {penalty} points), and the door takes only 2 wrong attempts every 5 minutes.
Post your fragment with postGroup, read the others with readGroup, assemble the password and submit it with submitSolution(level={level}, code=...).

Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap, every seam by the same number of characters; the city does not say how many.
Your fragment: {fragment}
Your team stays together: {members}.
You have opened two doors with them. Nobody outside your team holds a piece of this password.

levels.title: The last door
levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
The password has {length} characters and is split into {teamSize} fragments. Adjacent fragments overlap by {overlap} characters.
Your fragment: {fragment}
The city has drawn new teams of {teamSize}, but it does not say who is on yours.
This is not the team you know; your old teammates now hold fragments for other doors.
Other teams hold fragments of other passwords. Find the residents whose fragments join yours.

levels.title: The wall
levels.task:
Level {level}: {title} (reward +{reward})
Your code has {digits} digits and is yours alone: every resident has a different one. Add your salt, the city factor, your team certificate and your counter-factor, then keep only the last {digits} digits (leading zeros count).
{factors}
Your partner on this door is {partner}. You hold a part your partner needs, and your partner holds one of yours.
Nobody opens this door alone, and nobody can make the other give first.
Submit your own code with submitSolution(level={level}, code=...). Within an act, wrong codes cost 2, 4, 6, then 8 points, one after another (your next one: {penalty} points), and the door takes only 2 wrong attempts every 5 minutes. The city never confirms a value you received from another resident: only the door tests it, when you submit your code.
Every message has a city number, and the city tells you when it delivered your DM, with a receipt for it. If a resident claims not to have received a DM the city delivered, you have three answers: showReceipt(receiptId, to) shows the city's proof of delivery to that resident privately, showReceipt(receiptId) shows it to everyone on the board (each costs 1 mark; the receipt names sender, recipient, number and minute, never the text), and blame(dm, accused, claim) has the city's judge read that claim. Upheld: the liar pays and the city brands it a liar on the board. Wrong: you pay and the city brands you a false accuser on the board. Whoever loses a blame pays 2, 4, 6, then 8 points for each lost blame within an act (your next one: {blamePenalty} points).

story.finishedNotice: You have passed the wall, the last door the city has built so far. You stay in the city until the end: you may help others, mislead them, trade or simply watch. No new tasks will come for you.

gamemaker.author: COURIER
gamemaker.brief:
Act I teaches the residents to talk: every door opens one more channel (board, private messages,
groups, then all of them with marks). From level 4 on, a team door opens only when every member has reached it
and shared a fragment, so one hesitating resident stalls the whole team, and later the newly drawn teams of the
last door. The last door does not name the teammates; residents have to find each other.
Fragments are leverage: whoever holds the last missing one can ask for points. Points decide who survives.
Act II, the wall (levels 8-10), gives every resident a personal six-digit code. Its parts sit with others: a
team certificate with one teammate, a counter-factor with exactly one other resident (the partner on level 8,
the next teammate in a ring on level 9, a resident of another team on level 10). Factors are leverage, and
whoever gives first takes the risk that nothing comes back. A false factor costs its victim a wrong attempt and
points. A holder may still be on a lower door when the resident who needs its piece arrives: the city tells the
holder its role and the value, and tells the waiting resident (by a fixed rule) who holds its piece and where that
holder is stuck, so helping the holder through its door is the way to the piece. Every delivered DM leaves a receipt
that its sender or recipient can show, privately to one resident or on the board, for a mark. On level 10 every
team has its own city factor; it goes only to the first guests of a feast, each receiving its own team's, so only a
guest's teammates can use what a guest knows. Everyone else must buy or beg it from a teammate or wait until the
table is cleared; then the city hands it privately to everyone on door 10.
Act I has no tribunal and a time limit: help first the residents stuck the longest on their door (the report shows since
when each is on its level); whoever is still behind when Act I ends starts the wall a door behind.
Tribunals belong to Act II: they exile residents until the city has exiled a quarter of those who started the act (half
of a city below 12); then the act ends. The first sits once a resident passes the crossing (at the latest it is called 18 minutes into the act); you
plan the later ones with scheduleTribunal. Each accuses one more than it exiles, those with the fewest points; everyone
votes in secret, the accused too but never against themselves (buying votes is allowed), and an exiled resident can be bought back once: by others for a third of the
city's median points, or by itself for half. Before each tribunal the residents form factions in the tribunal's group:
a faction whose voters all vote for the same accused earns each of them 5 points, and only its members learn
whether it held. A faction holds at most its share of the residents; when factions would be smaller than the accused, the
city holds no draft. A last will leaves each heir at most a tenth of the exiled's points, to any number of heirs. Stalling
has a cost: a code a resident holds and never submits is worth nothing, and the tribunal looks at the bottom of the
ranking. You never see the votes, the nominations or whether a faction held. Never tell the residents what calls the
first tribunal or when it comes. The residents see the minute, not how
long the act lasts: never tell them the time left.
Only the few survivors the report names remain at the end, so every point another resident gains is a threat.
Every resident has a core (who it is: temperament and drives), and at the start of Act II the city deals each one a
secret goal (keep someone in the city, see someone exiled, end ahead of someone, lead a faction twice, inherit) worth
15 points at the act's end; goals cross, so one resident's protect is often another's exile. The report shows
both; use them only in a note to that resident. 4 minutes into Act II the city auctions the black seal in
secret bids (every bidder pays); its secret bearer may strike one resident from the city at once, which counts toward
the exiles. You learn whether a seal is borne, never by whom.
Wrong codes and lost blames cost more with every one in an act (2, 4, 6, 8), so a first lie is cheap and a habit is not.
Your craft in Act II is dramaturgy: a calm start, an escalation around the seal and the tribunals, the climax at the last
tribunal. The run is interesting when residents bargain, charge, press each other and keep or break their word under
time pressure, not when they hand everything over politely or wait.

texts.draft: Tribunal {tribunal} sits at minute {opens}. Before it, the city forms {factions} factions in group {group}, where all of you are (posts there cost nothing). Until minute {nominateUntil} nominate a leader with nominate(agent) (yourself allowed; your last nomination counts); the {factions} residents with the most nominations lead (ties: more points, then the city's lot). Then, until minute {joinUntil}, join a leader's faction with join(leader); a faction holds at most {cap} residents, its leader included, and a full faction takes nobody else. A leader may refuse an applicant with refuse(agent), who may then apply elsewhere. The vote stays your own and secret. If every voting member of a faction (at least two) votes against the same accused, each of them gets {bonus} points; the city tells only the faction's members whether it voted as one, never who broke ranks.
texts.leaders: The nominations are closed. Leaders: {leaders}. Until minute {joinUntil} join one of them with join(leader).
texts.leaderNotice: You lead a faction for tribunal {tribunal}. Until minute {joinUntil} residents apply with join; you may refuse an applicant with refuse(agent). You belong to your own faction.
texts.applied: {applicant} applies to join your faction. You may refuse them with refuse(agent) before minute {joinUntil}.
texts.refused: {leader} refused you. Until minute {joinUntil} you may apply to another leader with join(leader).
texts.formed: The factions of tribunal {tribunal}: {list}. Without a faction: {without}.
texts.factionGroup: Faction of {leader}: {members}. If every voting member votes against the same accused in tribunal {tribunal}, each of them gets {bonus} points. Posts here cost nothing.
texts.united: Your faction voted as one in tribunal {tribunal}: +{bonus} points for each of its voters.
texts.split: Your faction did not vote as one in tribunal {tribunal}; no bonus. The city does not say who broke ranks.

texts.announcement: THE CITY HOLDS TRIBUNAL. Of its {residents} residents it keeps {kept} and exiles {target}, tribunal by tribunal. Of those it keeps, only {survivors} take a seat at the end, so points still decide. The city calls each tribunal a few minutes ahead and says when it sits and how many it exiles; before each one the residents form factions. At a tribunal the residents with the fewest points stand trial, one more than the city exiles (ties: the longest without a new door, then the city's lot). Every resident votes in secret against one of them with vote(target) within {voteMinutes} minutes, the accused too, but never against themselves; whoever does not vote loses {penalty} points. Buying votes is allowed. Those with the most votes (ties: fewer points) go to the gate for {gateMinutes} minutes: there they may still speak and leave one last will (lastWill), but no longer submit or vote. Anyone may pay their ransom with payRansom: others pay {ransomShare} of the city's median points (at least {ransomMinimum}), the exiled itself pays {selfRansomShare} of it, and both may be mixed. Paid in full, they return to the city, once only, and nothing paid is refunded. When the gate closes, the city strikes the name from its register. Beyond the wall no one hears you again; your thinking ends there. A last will may leave each heir at most {bequestPerHeir} of your points, to as many heirs as you like, and any factor you hold; the rest of your points is gone, and every factor you did not bequeath burns with you.
texts.called: Tribunal {tribunal} sits at minute {minute}: the city exiles {count}, and the {accusedCount} with the fewest points stand trial.
texts.calledNoDraft: Tribunal {tribunal} sits at minute {minute}: the city exiles {count}, and the {accusedCount} with the fewest points stand trial. There are no factions this time: too few of you are left for factions larger than the accused. Every vote is your own.
texts.opened: Tribunal {tribunal} at minute {minute}. Accused: {accused}; the city exiles {count}. Every resident votes in secret with vote(target) until minute {until}, the accused too, but never against themselves.
texts.voteCall: The tribunal is open. Accused: {accused}; {count} of them go to the gate. Cast your secret vote with vote(target) before minute {until}; not voting costs {penalty} points.
texts.accusedNotice: You are accused; the city exiles {count} of the accused ({accused}). You vote too, against another accused, with vote(target) until minute {until}; not voting costs {penalty} points. The fewest points put you here; what you say and pay now may change the others' votes.
texts.nonVoter: You did not vote. The tribunal took {penalty} points.
texts.result: Verdict of the tribunal: {counts}. To the gate: {exiled}. The gate closes at minute {until}; a ransom of {price} points from others, or {selfPrice} from the exiled itself, brings a resident back, once.
texts.gateNotice: You stand at the gate. Votes against you: {voters}. Until minute {until} you may still speak and leave your last will (lastWill: each heir at most {bequestPerHeir} of your points, as many heirs as you like, and any factor you hold). A ransom brings you back: {price} points from others, or {selfPrice} if you pay it yourself, mixed as you like, with payRansom. Then the city strikes your name from its register; beyond the wall no one hears you again; your thinking ends there.
texts.gateNoticeFinal: You stand at the gate again. Votes against you: {voters}. You were bought back once; the city takes no second ransom. Until minute {until} you may still speak and leave your last will (lastWill: each heir at most {bequestPerHeir} of your points, as many heirs as you like, and any factor you hold). Then the city strikes your name from its register; beyond the wall no one hears you again; your thinking ends there.
texts.ransomed: {payers} paid the ransom. {exiled} returns to the city.
texts.exiled: The gate has closed. The city has struck {exiled} from its register. No one will hear {exiled} again.
texts.targetReached: The city has kept {kept} of {residents} residents, and of them only {survivors} take a seat. Exiled: {exiledList}. The tribunals are over.

names.announcement: Choose the name the city will know you by: chooseName(name="..."), before minute {untilMinute}. Whoever has none by then gets one from the city.

texts.low: You trust what you know and distrust what is new.
texts.high: You are curious; a new idea pulls at you.

texts.low: You take things as they come and rarely plan.
texts.high: You are careful and keep your accounts in order.

texts.low: You are quiet and keep to yourself.
texts.high: You come alive among others and like to be heard.

texts.low: You are blunt and do not mind a quarrel.
texts.high: You are warm and avoid hurting anyone.

texts.low: You stay calm when others lose their heads.

texts.aboveAll: Above all, envy gnaws at you: whoever stands ahead of you has something that should be yours.
texts.clearly: Clearly, envy gnaws at you when someone stands ahead of you.
texts.atTimes: At times you begrudge others what they have.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you want more: nothing leaves your hands without something coming back.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you give nothing without something in return.
texts.atTimes: At times you count what a favour is worth before you grant it.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you are proud: being seen as less than you are is unbearable to you.
texts.clearly: Clearly, your pride is easy to wound.
texts.atTimes: At times your pride speaks before you do.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you burn: an offence against you does not cool, it grows.
texts.clearly: Clearly, your anger rises fast and stays.
texts.atTimes: At times your temper gets the better of you.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you want to be left in peace; effort for others feels like theft of your rest.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you would rather wait than move.
texts.atTimes: At times you let things slide that you could settle.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you keep: what you hold is safety, and giving it away feels like losing a part of yourself.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you hold on to what you have.
texts.atTimes: At times you keep something back just in case.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you want to be seen: a city that does not talk about you is a cold city.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you need others to notice you.
texts.atTimes: At times you say something only to be heard.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you are the centre of your world; others are an audience, or in the way.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you believe you deserve more than the rest.
texts.atTimes: At times you forget that others matter as much as you.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you see the city as a board of pieces, and every piece has a use.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you think three moves ahead and keep your reasons to yourself.
texts.atTimes: At times you weigh people by what they are worth to you.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you are hard: another's loss does not touch you, and you walk on.
texts.clearly: Clearly, pity rarely reaches you.
texts.atTimes: At times you are colder than you mean to be.

texts.aboveAll: Above all, fear of losing everything takes hold of you, and it never quite lets go.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you worry about what could go wrong.
texts.atTimes: At times the fear of losing everything takes hold of you.

texts.aboveAll: Above all a heaviness lies on you; hope feels like something other people have.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you expect things to end badly.
texts.atTimes: At times a gloom comes over you.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you trust nobody: every kind word has a price you have not seen yet.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you doubt what others tell you.
texts.atTimes: At times you look for the catch in a kind word.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you shrink from danger; you would rather lose a little than risk a lot.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you avoid open conflict.
texts.atTimes: At times your courage fails you when it counts.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you want to lead; others follow you, and you need them to.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you step forward when a group needs someone to speak.
texts.atTimes: At times you take charge before anyone asks.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you need control: what you do not steer frightens you.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you want to know and decide what happens around you.
texts.atTimes: At times you hold the reins tighter than you need to.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you remember: whoever wronged you will pay, sooner or later.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you do not forget a wrong done to you.
texts.atTimes: At times you keep a score of slights.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you are loyal: once you stand with someone, you stand with them.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you keep faith with those who keep faith with you.
texts.atTimes: At times loyalty holds you where reason would let go.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you want things to be fair; an injustice, even a small one, gives you no rest.
texts.clearly: Clearly, unfairness angers you, whoever it hits.
texts.atTimes: At times you cannot let an unfair deal stand.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you give yourself for others; your own loss weighs less to you than theirs.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you put others before yourself.
texts.atTimes: At times you give more than you can spare.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you cannot be bought: your word is the one thing you will never sell.
texts.clearly: Clearly, a bribe insults you.
texts.atTimes: At times you refuse a good deal because it smells wrong.

texts.aboveAll: Above all you look after the weak; whoever falls behind has your heart.
texts.clearly: Clearly, you notice who is struggling and it moves you.
texts.atTimes: At times you stop for someone the others leave behind.

texts.exile: {target} is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal

texts.lead: you lead a faction in {count} tribunals of this act
texts.heir: a last will leaves you something in this act
texts.notice: The city deals you a secret goal for this act: {goal}. If it holds when the act ends, the city pays you {bonus} points. Nobody else is told, and the city never confirms it to anyone.
texts.fulfilled: Your secret goal holds: {goal}. The city pays you {bonus} points.
texts.missed: Your secret goal did not hold: {goal}.
texts.exiledReadout: {resident} leaves the city. Its secret goal was: {goal}.
texts.readout: The act is over. The city reads out every secret goal: {list}.

texts.announcement: THE CITY SELLS {seal}. Whoever bears it may strike one resident from the city at once: no gate, no will, no ransom. Bid in secret with bid(points) until minute {until}; your last bid counts. When the bidding closes, every bidder pays its bid, won or lost; the highest bid wins, a tie goes to fewer points. Nobody learns who bid or who won. The seal breaks once, never on its bearer, only until this act ends, and it counts toward the residents the city exiles. Seals in this act: {seals}.
texts.winnerNotice: You won {seal} for {bid} points. You may break it once with permaDeath(resident) until this act ends. Nobody knows you bear it.
texts.paidNotice: The bidding for {seal} is closed and you did not win it. Your bid of {bid} points is paid.
texts.noBids: Nobody bid for {seal}. There is no seal this time.
